sources.title: MIVUBI Movement Velocity Knockback and Physics State Policy v1

facts.subject: player/entity physics state
facts.statement: Critical transitions should declare expected physics state covering velocity policy, grounded/airborne expectation where relevant, knockback/impulse ownership, movement/input lock interaction, fall/void recovery, and arena spatial bounds.

facts.subject: teleport transition
facts.statement: Every critical teleport must explicitly choose whether velocity is preserved, cleared, or replaced by a known vector; leaving this implicit is prohibited when residual motion could violate spatial safety or life-state semantics.

facts.subject: void/fall recovery
facts.statement: Anti-void and out-of-bounds recovery should clear or intentionally normalize dangerous downward/horizontal momentum before or during safe return unless mode design explicitly preserves it; recovery is incomplete until post-teleport velocity is verified.

facts.subject: gameplay knockback
facts.statement: Scripted knockback/impulse should have an owning combat or gameplay operation plus arenaGeneration and entity/player generation. Stale knockback callbacks must not affect replacement entities or later rounds.

facts.subject: arena boundary knockback
facts.statement: Knockback that can move an entity/player outside its arena containment volume must be treated as a spatial-containment risk and validated against combat scope and boundary policy.

facts.subject: stuck detection
facts.statement: Before classifying an entity as navigation-stuck, inspect velocity/physics context. Low displacement during active knockback, airborne motion, collision pushing, or forced movement is not equivalent to pathfinding deadlock.

facts.subject: player movement restriction
facts.statement: Disabling movement input does not imply zero physical velocity. Input locks and physics state are separate surfaces; cutscene/downed/setup flows that require a stationary player must verify or normalize velocity independently.

facts.subject: revive/respawn physics
facts.statement: Revive and respawn flows must define a motion baseline. Health/life restoration does not prove momentum, airborne/fall context, or knockback state is safe for resumed gameplay.

facts.subject: mounted movement
facts.statement: If gameplay supports mounts/vehicles, teleport/recovery/reset must explicitly define rider-vehicle handling and ownership; moving only one side of the relationship can leave inconsistent location or control state.

facts.subject: knockback compatibility
facts.statement: Knockback/pushability diagnostics must consult the effective runtime/format profile because recent component semantics changed across 1.26.x; behavior regressions after update should not be attributed solely to arena logic.

facts.subject: physics transition commit
facts.statement: After critical teleport, recovery, revive, scripted impulse, or reset, verify current location, containment, and velocity satisfy the transition contract before dependent gameplay commits.
